subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session webhook deliveries be rejected with 409, queued/serialized, or left parallel by default, and should that behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent overlap contract changes external HTTP retry semantics and session-state behavior for existing integrations, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as skip, queue, or parallel while preserving today's default async acceptance for existing callers.

options.title: Unconditional 409 guard
options.body: Implement the reporter's exact behavior for every same-session active hook delivery and accept the compatibility break for callers expecting 200/runId.

options.title: Fold into queued webhooks
options.body: Defer this guard until the queued-webhook design chooses durable backlog, per-queue parallelism, and caller response semantics together.

recommendation.title: Opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit hook or mapping policy such as skip, queue, or parallel while preserving today's default async acceptance for existing callers.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest product/security routing signal from adjacent hook session-key hardening and prior review framing for this exact policy boundary.
